pxPerFoot.note: Spec 3.5: one 8-foot length is 32 px, the width of the horse frame.

hoofBaseY.note: Hoof line of lane 0. Lanes 0 to 8 give y116 to y148.

gateScreenX.note: World x 0, the start line, sits here during the gate beat. Must equal leaderScreenX so the camera does not jump on the break.

finalFeetToGo.note: The 1/16 pole. The camera hands over to the leaders from here.

finalBlendSeconds.note: Race seconds over which the camera blends to the wire.

finalCatchUpPxPerSecond.note: Most the blend may add per race second over the race camera, so a horse far back does not make the camera jump more than 32 px a frame at 2x (RV5).

midZonePadPx.note: Mid-layer px the grandstand runs past each end of a stretch, so it still fills the screen with the camera locked on the wire.

strideFeet.note: Feet per gallop cycle. A thoroughbred's stride is roughly 20 to 25 feet, from memory, not checked.

stridePhasePerPost.note: Share of a cycle each program number shifts the gallop, so the field never moves in lockstep.

frameTopFromHoof.note: Frame top = hoof y - 23 (24 px frame, hoof on its last row).

playerArrowDx.note: DESIGN stand-in: the 7x4 arrow centered over the cap (x20-24), so its left column is frame x19.

playerArrowDy.note: Bottom row 2 px above the frame top: rows frame y-6 to y-3.

speed.note: Spec 3.4: a 2:01.55 race plays in about 61 seconds.

fastSpeed.note: While Space is held, during the race only.

maxFrameMs.note: A stalled tab does not jump the race.

pickSeconds.note: Was the P0 pick window (4 s) while keys 1 to 8 picked a horse at the gate. The card screen picks from step 5, so it is 0 and the gate beat is the spec's length. Kept so the window can come back without a schema change.

gateStillSeconds.note: The field stands still, then the doors swap open and the race clock starts.

photoSeconds.note: Spec 4.3 and 4.4: the whole photo, 1.5 s to look and 3.0 s with the caption. Only when the result flags a photo.

photoCaptionSeconds.note: Spec 4.4: "Photo finish" alone this long from the photo's start, then the winner line. The photo ends photoSeconds minus this after the winner line shows.

maxSequenceSeconds.note: The brief's cap on sim plus animation for a 10-furlong race.

frameLeft.note: DESIGN Charm: the winner's frame at screen x112-143.

slowSeconds.note: Wall seconds the background takes to slow from the winner's speed at the wire to a walk; walk frames and the fist from then on.

walkPxPerSecond.note: About 6 feet a second at 4 px a foot, a brisk walk in real time.

walkStrideFeet.note: Feet per walk cycle, so the feet do not slide. From memory, not checked.

stepPx.note: Spec 4.4: the panel steps in from the top by whole 8 px moves, 25 of them.

stepsPerSecond.note: One move a frame at 60 Hz, timed by the wall clock so a 120 Hz screen steps at the same speed.

repeatDelayMs.note: Spec 5: a held arrow on the card or Orders repeats after this long.

entryBand.note: DESIGN Program pages: the highlighter band behind a program entry on the Card and Orders, from 1 row above the entry to 1 below. Rows split into four groups, extra rows to the top; group g's first column is x0 + leftSteps[g], its last x1 - rightSteps[g] (chisel ends).

resultBand.note: DESIGN Program pages: your order row on the Result, the row's 8 rows plus 1 above and 1 below.

swipeHalfX1.note: DESIGN Program pages: the swipe's frame 1 is the band from x0 to here, with the chisel end at this end.

swipeFrame2Seconds.note: The whole band and the tick, held, then the cut to Orders.

rows.note: The Orders screen's paddock strip, y144-191, top row first: y144-159 rail, y160-175 ground, y176-191 ground, each tile repeated 16 times across, so the planks (y153-154, y157-158) sit above the trainer and your horse. The rail flips every odd tile (flipX when floor(x / 16) is odd), as the race rails do, so its 2 px posts come every 32 px. From the artist and art-director, 2026-11-13.

trainerAt.note: Spec 4.2: the trainer's 16x24 frame's top-left; its boots land on y187.

horseAt.note: Spec 4.2: your horse's 32x24 stand frame's top-left.

cupDownSeconds.note: DESIGN Charm: the trainer's cup is down 1.5 s, then up 0.5 s.

cap.note: DESIGN Charm cap: at most 3 ambient things moving while the field runs.

flagSwapsPerSecond.note: DESIGN: the flag swaps every 0.4 s.

cursorSwapsPerSecond.note: DESIGN: the horseshoe cursor bobs 0.5 s a frame.

backInStrideSeconds.note: Playback seconds after your horse's event.

typeUntilFurlongsToGo.note: Calls type out before this pole and cut in whole from it (the 1/8 pole).

poleBands.note: Kentucky 810 KAR 2:070 Section 6(1): red and white quarter poles, green and white eighth poles, black and white sixteenth poles (found by the artist 2026-11-12). Black is Coal, not Ink, so the band never merges with the Ink outline. Joseph has not confirmed it.

saddlecloths.note: Numbers 1 to 8, from DESIGN.md. The US convention from memory, to check against a primary source before it ships.

early.default: Let this one break and find its own rhythm.
early.rateEarly: Take a hold early. Let the speed horses argue up front.

move.default: Ask when it feels right. You know this one.
move.moveAtThreeEighths: Go at the 3/8 pole. It's a long run home, so mean it.
move.saveForStretch: Sit chilly till the stretch. Then ask for everything.

path.default: Take whatever path opens. Going around is fine.
path.stayInside: Hug the rail. Save the ground and hope it opens.

trainer.go: Good luck. I'll be at the rail with the coffee.
trainer.back: Want a different horse? No hard feelings.

backstretch: Down the back side they go
